# Marginal prices and execution averages

The displayed next price and the cost of a whole order answer different questions\.

Ask is what you pay to buy; bid is what the market pays when you sell\. In the regional scenario each unit changes public stock, so later units in a large order may have different prices\.

The exact total adds the actual prices across the complete order\. Average execution price is that total divided by quantity for display\. Neither average nor the first marginal price replaces the exact total used for payment\.

An automation price limit applies to the worst marginal unit in its selected order\. A profitable\-looking current quote does not guarantee the same price after a voyage, production, consumption, or another merchant's trade\.

Modern circulation Coverage pricing protects Furniture with a two\-good target floor even when luxury purchases are suspended\. Actual stock and each town's reference price still determine bid and ask; the target creates neither demand nor goods\. Older runs retain their original prices\.
